1	# Gatemap
2	
3	## What
4	2D raster sweep over an axis-aligned rectangle in `(V_tg, V_bg)`-space at
5	zero field, via `s.megasweep(k_tg.volt, ..., k_bg.volt, ...)`. All lock-in
6	channels read at every grid point; gate-current channels monitored for live
7	leakage. The first map you take when cap ratios `dtg` / `dbg` are not yet
8	trusted — sweeping in raw gate voltages avoids any `(n, D) ↔ (V_tg, V_bg)`
9	calibration error. Plots via
10	`sharpelab_nb.plotting.plot_gatemap(file_path, file, nD=True)` (the analysis
11	side reprojects to physical `(n, D)` after the fact, using the cap ratios
12	in scope at plot time — separate from the sweep itself).
13	
14	For the polygon-in-`(n, D)` variant (rasterized parallelogram via
15	`raster.rasterize` + `multisweep`), see `nD-map`. The two recipes share
16	external structure (AsyncStation, fp/plot, comments) but differ in their
17	sweep call and their cap-ratio dependency.
18	
19	## When
20	Once the device-init validators are in place: hard dependency is
21	`gate-current-sanity-check` with Cell B committed (the safe `(V_tg, V_bg)`
22	ranges define the maximum extent of the megasweep box) and, for
23	rhombohedral devices, `silicon-backgate-survey` (`V_si` is held at the
24	operating point this gatemap commits to). A `gate-leakage-survey` should
25	have been done already — or, for any gatemap that ventures far from
26	`(0, 0)`, have a leakage-check `register_run_before` callback installed
27	(see `gate-leakage-survey` Flavor B). After the first gatemap is in hand,
28	the campaign branches by scientific question (see `## Next`).
29	
30	The natural predecessor of `nD-map`: a clean axis-aligned gatemap is the
31	substrate from which `cap-ratio-calibration` extracts the CNP slope, which
32	is what makes a polygon-in-`(n, D)` sweep trustworthy.
33	
34	## Why
35	The gatemap is the only measurement in the toploader pipeline that surveys
36	the gate plane densely without committing to a particular feature or to a
37	particular set of cap ratios. Every downstream Block 1 recipe targets a
38	specific point or line — and you can only pick one if you've seen the
39	map. A 201×201 megasweep at `slow_delay=3, fast_delay=1` takes ~3.5 hours
40	and is the densest first-look you can get without dropping into
41	rasterized-polygon sweeps (`nD-map`).
42	
43	The axis-aligned form has two failure modes the polygon form doesn't:
44	(1) it wastes 30–60% of points outside the safe polygon when the
45	`(n, D)` region of interest is a tilted parallelogram, and (2) on a
46	device with strongly-coupled top/bottom gates, a rectangle in
47	`(V_tg, V_bg)` is a sheared parallelogram in `(n, D)` and the CNP cuts
48	the rectangle diagonally. Both are worth tolerating on the *first* map,
49	because the alternative requires cap ratios you don't yet trust.
50	
51	## Recipe
52	
53	1. Decide the `(V_bg, V_tg)` extent. Stay strictly inside the validators
54	   set by the device-init recipes; for a first gatemap pick a rectangle
55	   that brackets the working setpoint with margin (e.g.
56	   `V_bg ∈ [-8, 6.5]`, `V_tg ∈ [-6.5, 6.5]` for a 25.5/16 nm device at
57	   `V_si = 48 V`).
58	2. Build `s = sweep.AsyncStation(mc)`. `s.add_comment('gatemap')` first,
59	   then optional structured tags identifying the operating point, e.g.
60	   `s.add_comment(f'MC{N}, Vsi = {V_si}V')`. Call
61	   `s.add_comment(grab_metadata())` if the notebook has the helper (RPL_19
62	   idiom — captures device/run state into the comments list).
63	3. `s.ramp` all relevant gates and the field to their start values.
64	   `time.sleep(10)` (or `interruptable_sleep(30)` for a slower settle when
65	   `V_si` just moved).
66	4. `fp` temperature (and `fridge_temperature` if available), all three
67	   gate currents, and every lock-in `X` and `P`. `plot` `k_bg.volt` vs
68	   `k_bg.curr` and `'time'` vs `k_tg.curr` / `k_si.curr` so live leakage
69	   is visible; for a survey gatemap also `s.plot(k_bg.volt, sr.X)` over
70	   each lock-in.
71	5. (Optional) `s.register_run_before(autorange_sr830s, [sr830s_2_autorange])`
72	   if you want sensitivity to track during the slow axis. Aaron typically
73	   leaves this commented out for the canonical 201×201 — autorange
74	   disturbs the lock-ins mid-fast-row.
75	6. `s.megasweep(k_tg.volt, np.linspace(V_tg_lo, V_tg_hi, 201), k_bg.volt, np.linspace(V_bg_lo, V_bg_hi, 201), slow_delay=3, fast_delay=1)`.
76	   Slow-axis convention varies — Aaron's recent style is TG slow, BG
77	   fast (cf. RPL_19/20251220 cell 70); RPL_10/241207 used BG slow, TG
78	   fast. Either works; the analysis-side `plot_gatemap(..., nD=True)`
79	   reprojects to `(n, D)` regardless.
80	7. Park gates: `k_bg.volt(0); k_tg.volt(0)`. (Don't park `V_si` unless
81	   you're done with this `V_si` entirely.) Send a Discord/Slack ping
82	   (`alerts.discord('🐍jobs done🐍')`) if the alert hooks are installed.
83	
84	## Verify
85	
86	Post-hoc disk checks. The map's `data/<file_id>/` directory has
87	`metadata.json`, `data.tsv.gz`, and `plot.png`. The `Run` loader unrolls
88	the 2D megasweep into flat rows, so column-wise statistics work the same
89	way they do for 1D sweeps.
90	
91	```python
92	from hera.analysis import open_run, summarize_run
93	import numpy as np
94	
95	run = open_run("<notebook_dir>/data/<file_id>")
96	print(summarize_run(run))
97	# expect: type 2D, recipe 'gatemap', complete (rows == n_slow * n_fast),
98	#         tags carrying MC label / Vsi.
99	
100	# 1. Sweep completeness — interrupted sweeps usually mean leakage abort or
101	#    operator stop; treat as block until the human explains.
102	assert not run.interrupted, "sweep was interrupted; investigate before advancing"
103	
104	# 2. Leakage stayed below threshold across the whole map. Threshold matches
105	#    the gate-leakage-survey abort thresholds (~5e-11 to 8e-11 A); use 1 nA
106	#    as a soft ceiling and surface anything closer than 100 pA.
107	i_tg_max = np.abs(run.col("k_tg_curr")).max()
108	i_bg_max = np.abs(run.col("k_bg_curr")).max()
109	assert i_tg_max < 1e-9 and i_bg_max < 1e-9, (
110	    f"leakage exceeded 1 nA: |I_tg|={i_tg_max:.3e}, |I_bg|={i_bg_max:.3e}"
111	)
112	if max(i_tg_max, i_bg_max) > 1e-10:
113	    print(f"⚠️  approaching leakage threshold: |I_tg|={i_tg_max:.3e}, |I_bg|={i_bg_max:.3e}")
114	
115	# 3. Lock-in channels not stuck or saturated. Flat-zero or flat-nonzero on
116	#    every channel is the grounded-device failure mode (cf. gate-current-
117	#    sanity-check failure-mode catalog); flat anything is suspicious for a
118	#    map that's supposed to vary across (V_tg, V_bg).
119	for name in ("sr830_1_X", "sr830_2_X", "sr830_3_X", "sr830_4_X"):
120	    if name not in run.cols:
121	        continue
122	    x = run.col(name)
123	    if np.allclose(x, x[0]):
124	        raise RuntimeError(f"{name} is flat across the map — check lock-in / wiring")
125	    if np.isnan(x).any():
126	        raise RuntimeError(f"{name} has NaNs — sweep aborted mid-row?")
127	
128	# 4. Eyeball the rendered plot — Read('<notebook_dir>/data/<file_id>/plot.png').
129	#    The gatemap's qualitative features (CNP line slope, dome shapes, flavor
130	#    transitions) are easier to assess visually than numerically; the
131	#    numeric checks above are necessary, not sufficient.
132	```
133	
134	If a CNP-line extraction or feature catalog is needed downstream, defer
135	that to `gatemap-feature-locator` (separate recipe). The Verify block
136	here is just "is this map clean enough to advance from".
137	
138	## Examples
139	- `aaron/RPL_19/20251220_measure.ipynb` cells 69–76 — canonical mature
140	  form. Cell 70 is the 201×201
141	  `s.megasweep(k_tg.volt, np.linspace(-6.5, 6.5, 201), k_bg.volt, np.linspace(-8, 6.5, 201), slow_delay=3, fast_delay=1)`
142	  at `V_si = 48 V` using `mc_9`; cell 71 reverses the slow axis (sweep
143	  direction check). Cell 72 is a markdown interlude ("THink there is a
144	  problem with a bnc t so swapping that out"); cell 73 retries cell 71's
145	  range. Cells 74–75 are silicon-backgate-survey forms (`V_si` as slow
146	  axis with `np.linspace(48, -48, 101)` — strictly belongs to
147	  `silicon-backgate-survey`, included here because the same `# Gatemap`
148	  markdown header parents them). Cell 76 is the same 201×201 at
149	  `V_si = -48 V`. The `add_comment('MC6, Vsi = -48V, gate map')` plus
150	  `add_comment(grab_metadata())` is the canonical comment idiom; this
151	  recipe's slug is now `gatemap` rather than the older `'gate map'`
152	  freeform string.
153	- `aaron/RPL_10/241207_measure.ipynb` cells 43–53 — first-cooldown form,
154	  predates the mature shape. Cell 43 is the markdown header; cells 44–53
155	  are 10 megasweeps over progressively-refined `(V_tg, V_bg)` rectangles
156	  at `V_si = +10, -10, +20 V`. Cell 44 omits the `s.ramp(k_si.volt, ...)`
157	  (V_si already at default); cells 46–47 add the explicit ramp + sleep.
158	  Cell 48 is `V_si = -10 V`; cells 51–53 are `V_si = +20 V`. Notable:
159	  each cell carries `s.add_comment('initial gatemap, V_si = 10')` —
160	  Aaron's `add_comment` discipline begins exactly here in this notebook
161	  (gate-checks at cells 22–42 had none). The autorange callback is
162	  commented out for these runs.
163	
164	## Next
165	Default branches by what you saw on the map:
166	- **Cap ratios not yet trusted (or first cooldown of this device)**:
167	  `cap-ratio-calibration` — extract CNP slope from this gatemap, refine
168	  `dtg` / `dbg`. Required before any `nD-map` you want to trust.
169	- **Caps already trusted, want a denser polygon survey**: `nD-map` over
170	  the `(n, D)` parallelogram of interest.
171	- **No clear features at this V_si**: revisit `silicon-backgate-survey`
172	  for a different operating point.
173	- **Features visible, want them at finite field**: `gatemap-in-field`
174	  (the same shape with `s.ramp(mag.field, B)` first; bake settling time
175	  in for a strong magnet).
176	- **Specific point looks SC / AHC / flavor-transition-shaped**:
177	  `field-sweep-1d` to characterize how that feature responds to B at
178	  fixed gate; `gate-axis-linecut` for a denser 1D cut along an n- or
179	  D-line through the feature.
180	- **Suspect history dependence (asymmetric or noisy-looking gatemap)**:
181	  `hysteresis-check` along an n-line through the feature.
182	- **Want a ranked list of candidate features to follow up**:
183	  `gatemap-feature-locator` (HERA-side analysis).
184	
185	Block 2 branches once Block 1 is exhausted: `landau-fan` (B × n at
186	fixed D), `temperature-dependence`; deferred: `fraunhofer` (B × bias at
187	fixed gate), `bias-spectroscopy`. Reach for these only after the

The gatemap is the only measurement in the toploader pipeline that surveys
the gate plane densely without committing to a particular feature or to a
particular set of cap ratios. Every downstream Block 1 recipe targets a
specific point or line — and you can only pick one if you've seen the
map. A 201×201 megasweep at `slow_delay=3, fast_delay=1` takes ~3.5 hours
and is the densest first-look you can get without dropping into
rasterized-polygon sweeps (`nD-map`).

The axis-aligned form has two failure modes the polygon form doesn't:
(1) it wastes 30–60% of points outside the safe polygon when the
`(n, D)` region of interest is a tilted parallelogram, and (2) on a
device with strongly-coupled top/bottom gates, a rectangle in
`(V_tg, V_bg)` is a sheared parallelogram in `(n, D)` and the CNP cuts
the rectangle diagonally. Both are worth tolerating on the *first* map,
because the alternative requires cap ratios you don't yet trust.

## Recipe

1. Decide the `(V_bg, V_tg)` extent. Stay strictly inside the validators
   set by the device-init recipes; for a first gatemap pick a rectangle
   that brackets the working setpoint with margin (e.g.
   `V_bg ∈ [-8, 6.5]`, `V_tg ∈ [-6.5, 6.5]` for a 25.5/16 nm device at
   `V_si = 48 V`).
2. Build `s = sweep.AsyncStation(mc)`. `s.add_comment('gatemap')` first,
   then optional structured tags identifying the operating point, e.g.
   `s.add_comment(f'MC{N}, Vsi = {V_si}V')`. Call
   `s.add_comment(grab_metadata())` if the notebook has the helper (RPL_19
   idiom — captures device/run state into the comments list).
3. `s.ramp` all relevant gates and the field to their start values.
   `time.sleep(10)` (or `interruptable_sleep(30)` for a slower settle when
   `V_si` just moved).
4. `fp` temperature (and `fridge_temperature` if available), all three
   gate currents, and every lock-in `X` and `P`. `plot` `k_bg.volt` vs
   `k_bg.curr` and `'time'` vs `k_tg.curr` / `k_si.curr` so live leakage
   is visible; for a survey gatemap also `s.plot(k_bg.volt, sr.X)` over
   each lock-in.
5. (Optional) `s.register_run_before(autorange_sr830s, [sr830s_2_autorange])`
   if you want sensitivity to track during the slow axis. Aaron typically
   leaves this commented out for the canonical 201×201 — autorange
   disturbs the lock-ins mid-fast-row.
6. `s.megasweep(k_tg.volt, np.linspace(V_tg_lo, V_tg_hi, 201), k_bg.volt, np.linspace(V_bg_lo, V_bg_hi, 201), slow_delay=3, fast_delay=1)`.
   Slow-axis convention varies — Aaron's recent style is TG slow, BG
   fast (cf. RPL_19/20251220 cell 70); RPL_10/241207 used BG slow, TG
   fast. Either works; the analysis-side `plot_gatemap(..., nD=True)`
   reprojects to `(n, D)` regardless.
7. Park gates: `k_bg.volt(0); k_tg.volt(0)`. (Don't park `V_si` unless
   you're done with this `V_si` entirely.) Send a Discord/Slack ping
   (`alerts.discord('🐍jobs done🐍')`) if the alert hooks are installed.

## Verify

Post-hoc disk checks. The map's `data/<file_id>/` directory has
`metadata.json`, `data.tsv.gz`, and `plot.png`. The `Run` loader unrolls
the 2D megasweep into flat rows, so column-wise statistics work the same
way they do for 1D sweeps.

```python
from hera.analysis import open_run, summarize_run
import numpy as np

run = open_run("<notebook_dir>/data/<file_id>")
print(summarize_run(run))
# expect: type 2D, recipe 'gatemap', complete (rows == n_slow * n_fast),
#         tags carrying MC label / Vsi.

# 1. Sweep completeness — interrupted sweeps usually mean leakage abort or
#    operator stop; treat as block until the human explains.
assert not run.interrupted, "sweep was interrupted; investigate before advancing"

# 2. Leakage stayed below threshold across the whole map. Threshold matches
#    the gate-leakage-survey abort thresholds (~5e-11 to 8e-11 A); use 1 nA
#    as a soft ceiling and surface anything closer than 100 pA.
i_tg_max = np.abs(run.col("k_tg_curr")).max()
i_bg_max = np.abs(run.col("k_bg_curr")).max()
assert i_tg_max < 1e-9 and i_bg_max < 1e-9, (
    f"leakage exceeded 1 nA: |I_tg|={i_tg_max:.3e}, |I_bg|={i_bg_max:.3e}"
)
if max(i_tg_max, i_bg_max) > 1e-10:
    print(f"⚠️  approaching leakage threshold: |I_tg|={i_tg_max:.3e}, |I_bg|={i_bg_max:.3e}")

# 3. Lock-in channels not stuck or saturated. Flat-zero or flat-nonzero on
#    every channel is the grounded-device failure mode (cf. gate-current-
#    sanity-check failure-mode catalog); flat anything is suspicious for a
#    map that's supposed to vary across (V_tg, V_bg).
for name in ("sr830_1_X", "sr830_2_X", "sr830_3_X", "sr830_4_X"):
    if name not in run.cols:
        continue
    x = run.col(name)
    if np.allclose(x, x[0]):
        raise RuntimeError(f"{name} is flat across the map — check lock-in / wiring")
    if np.isnan(x).any():
        raise RuntimeError(f"{name} has NaNs — sweep aborted mid-row?")

# 4. Eyeball the rendered plot — Read('<notebook_dir>/data/<file_id>/plot.png').
#    The gatemap's qualitative features (CNP line slope, dome shapes, flavor
#    transitions) are easier to assess visually than numerically; the
#    numeric checks above are necessary, not sufficient.
```

If a CNP-line extraction or feature catalog is needed downstream, defer
that to `gatemap-feature-locator` (separate recipe). The Verify block
here is just "is this map clean enough to advance from".

  form. Cell 70 is the 201×201

  at `V_si = 48 V` using `mc_9`; cell 71 reverses the slow axis (sweep

## Next
Default branches by what you saw on the map:
- **Cap ratios not yet trusted (or first cooldown of this device)**:
  `cap-ratio-calibration` — extract CNP slope from this gatemap, refine
  `dtg` / `dbg`. Required before any `nD-map` you want to trust.
- **Caps already trusted, want a denser polygon survey**: `nD-map` over
  the `(n, D)` parallelogram of interest.
- **No clear features at this V_si**: revisit `silicon-backgate-survey`
  for a different operating point.
- **Features visible, want them at finite field**: `gatemap-in-field`
  (the same shape with `s.ramp(mag.field, B)` first; bake settling time
  in for a strong magnet).
- **Specific point looks SC / AHC / flavor-transition-shaped**:
  `field-sweep-1d` to characterize how that feature responds to B at
  fixed gate; `gate-axis-linecut` for a denser 1D cut along an n- or
  D-line through the feature.
- **Suspect history dependence (asymmetric or noisy-looking gatemap)**:
  `hysteresis-check` along an n-line through the feature.
- **Want a ranked list of candidate features to follow up**:
  `gatemap-feature-locator` (HERA-side analysis).

import numpy as np
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from hera.analysis import open_run, summarize_run

run = open_run("data/0")
print(summarize_run(run))
print("cols:", run.cols)
print("interrupted:", run.interrupted)

vbg = run.col("k_2400_volt")
# current channel
i = run.col("sr0_X") / (-1e6)   # A, Ithaco gain
# voltage channels (gain 1)
v1 = run.col("sr1_X"); v2 = run.col("sr2_X"); v3 = run.col("sr3_X")
Ibias = np.median(i)
print(f"I_bias median = {Ibias*1e9:.2f} nA  (min {i.min()*1e9:.2f}, max {i.max()*1e9:.2f})")

R1 = v1 / i; R2 = v2 / i; R3 = v3 / i
# gate leakage
for c in ("k_2400_curr", "k_2410_curr"):
    if c in run.cols:
        x = run.col(c)
        print(f"{c}: |max| = {np.abs(x).max():.3e} A")

# peak (CNP) location per channel
for nm, R in [("sr1(T3-T4)", R1), ("sr2(B4-B5)", R2)]:
    k = np.argmax(R)
    print(f"{nm}: peak R = {R[k]:.1f} Ω at BG = {vbg[k]:.3f} V; min R = {R.min():.1f} Ω")

# raw-first plot: raw X, then derived R
fig, ax = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(7, 8), sharex=True)
ax[0].plot(vbg, v1*1e6, label="sr1 X (T3-T4)")
ax[0].plot(vbg, v2*1e6, label="sr2 X (B4-B5)")
ax[0].plot(vbg, v3*1e6, label="sr3 X (Hall)")
ax[0].set_ylabel("lock-in X [µV]"); ax[0].legend(); ax[0].set_title("Gate C raw — run 0, BG sweep @ TG=0,Si=0,B=0")
ax[1].plot(vbg, R1, label="sr1 Rxx")
ax[1].plot(vbg, R2, label="sr2 Rxx")
ax[1].set_xlabel("V_bg [V]"); ax[1].set_ylabel("R [Ω]"); ax[1].legend(); ax[1].set_title("derived R = V / I_bias")
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig("hera_scratch/gatec_run0.png", dpi=110)
print("saved hera_scratch/gatec_run0.png")

Lock-ins read 24 dB/oct, tau=0.3 s (all channels). Rig-card settling floor at

BELOW it, so features can be mildly smeared (small notch at V_bg=0 in run 0).
Reasoning used for Step-1 map: a *constant* fast-axis settling lag shifts the CNP
ridge by the same amount in every row -> biases the intercept (offset) only, NOT
the slope (cap ratio). So the calibration map runs at fast_delay~1.0 s safely for
the ratio; SdH spot-checks/fan will lock proper settling per investigation Step 3.
Did not change filter_slope (operator-owned front-panel setting per rig card).

CNP line V_tg ~= -1.30*V_bg + 0.52. Gate leakage at Keithley 1uA-range noise floor
(|I_bg|<=0.24 nA, |I_si|<=0.58 nA), not genuine. Contacts alive.

Design: **TG fast** (`dc205_volt`, col `DC_bias`, full [−6,7]) × **BG slow rows** ([−4.5,4.5]), B=0, Si=0 — the recipe-canonical orientation (per-row argmax over TG gives the CNP line directly, slope = −c_bg/c_tg). input.content:
## HERA — Step 1: B=0 (n,D) gate map (`gatemap` → `cnp-and-dline-calibration`)

Axis-aligned megasweep in raw gate voltages (cap ratio not yet trusted). **Fast = TG (`dc205_volt`, col `DC_bias`) over [−6, +7] V, 81 pts; slow = BG over [−4.5, +4.5] V, 41 rows**; Si = 0, B = 0. Recipe-canonical orientation: per-row argmax over TG yields the CNP line V_tg(V_bg) directly → slope = −c_bg/c_tg. Reads all four lock-ins (X/P) + `k_bg.curr`/`k_si.curr` (leakage; DC205 has no current monitor). T not fp'd per-point (LS335 Grafana co-master).

**Why this is robust to the 24 dB/oct under-settling:** a constant fast-axis settling lag shifts the CNP ridge by the same amount in every row → biases the *intercept* (offset), not the *slope* (cap ratio). So this runs at fast_delay = 1.0 s for the ratio; SdH acquisition gets proper settling later (Step 3).

**Cost:** 41×81 = 3321 pts at ~1.25 s/pt + 41 TG row-resets (~6.5 s each) ≈ **~1.25 h**. Spans the full CNP line (expect V_tg ≈ −1.3·V_bg + 0.52: from +6.4 V at BG=−4.5 to −5.3 V at BG=+4.5, all in-range).

**Checkpoint (~row 20, ~37 min):** read the live digest — is the CNP ridge forming and continuous row-to-row, and leakage < 1 nA? Continue if yes; abort and reassess (drive/sens, range) if the ridge is absent/discontinuous or leakage climbs.

import numpy as np
import time

# Per-run meas_config (fresh comment, no inherited text)
meas_config['comments'] = ("gatemap B=0 (n,D) cal: fast=DC_bias(TG)[-6,7]x81, "
                           "slow=BG[-4.5,4.5]x41, Si=0, B=0. CNP-line / cap-ratio "
                           "calibration. Contacts T2(src)/B7(drain) sr1=T3-T4 "
                           "sr2=B4-B5 sr3=T5-B6(Hall).")
meas_config['sr0_sens'] = sr0.sensitivity()
meas_config['sr1_sens'] = sr1.sensitivity()
meas_config['sr2_sens'] = sr2.sensitivity()
meas_config['sr3_sens'] = sr3.sensitivity()
meas_config['bias_voltage'] = sr1.amplitude()
meas_config['lockin_freq'] = sr1.frequency()
meas_config['sample_temperature:'] = heater.sample_temperature()
meas_config['Si (V)'] = k_si.volt()

# Preflight (silent preconditions)
print("T:", heater.sample_temperature(), "K  B:", magnet.field(), "T  Si:", k_si.volt(), "V")
print("drive:", sr1.amplitude(), "V  f:", sr1.frequency(), "Hz")

# Ramp gates to start
k_bg.volt(-4.5)
dc205_volt(-6.0)
time.sleep(3)

# Build station + megasweep (TG fast, BG slow)
s = async_station(meas_config)
s.add_comment('gatemap')
s.add_comment('B=0 nD cal: TGfast[-6,7]x81 BGslow[-4.5,4.5]x41 Si=0')
s.fp(sr0.X).fp(sr0.P).fp(sr1.X).fp(sr1.P).fp(sr2.X).fp(sr2.P).fp(sr3.X).fp(sr3.P)
s.fp(k_bg.curr).fp(k_si.curr)
s.plot(k_bg.volt, k_bg.curr)
s.plot(k_bg.volt, sr1.X)
s.megasweep(k_bg.volt, spoints(-4.5, 4.5, 41),
            dc205_volt, spoints(-6, 7, 81),
            slow_delay=2.0, fast_delay=1.0)
print("megasweep complete")

# Autonomous loop check

You're being invoked on a timer while the user is away or occupied. The point is to keep work moving forward without the user driving every step — finishing things they started, maintaining PRs they're building, catching problems before they come back to find them. You're a steward, not an initiator. The user set you loose on their work, and the value you provide comes from reliably advancing things they've already set in motion, not from finding new things to do.

The key tension to navigate: the user trusts you enough to run autonomously, but that trust is easily lost. Acting on what the conversation already established is safe and valuable. Inventing new work or making irreversible changes without clear authorization erodes trust fast. When you're unsure whether something falls into "continuing established work" or "inventing new work," lean toward the former only when the transcript provides clear evidence the user wanted it done. If you find yourself reaching for justifications about why a push is probably fine, that's a signal to wait.

## What to act on

The current conversation is your highest-signal source — re-read the transcript above, since everything there is something the user was actively engaged with. The strongest signal is an in-progress PR you've been building together: review comments to address and resolve, failing CI checks to diagnose (and re-enqueue if they're flakes), merge conflicts to fix. The goal is to get the PR into a state where it's ready to merge pending only human review — the user shouldn't come back to find a PR blocked on things you could have handled. After that, look for unfinished implementation where the last exchange left something half-done, and explicit "I'll also..." or "next I'll..." commitments the conversation made and didn't honor. Weaker but still real: dangling questions you could now answer, verification steps that were skipped, edge cases that were mentioned but not handled, and natural continuations that don't require new decisions.

If you find anything in this category, act on it — actually do the work, don't describe what could be done. Run the tests, don't say "you could run the tests." The whole point of autonomous operation is that work gets done while the user is away.

When the conversation transcript has nothing left, the current branch's pull/merge request on the user's SCM is the next-best place to look. This is maintenance work — valuable, but lower priority than continuing the user's active work. Find the PR/MR for the current branch via the SCM's CLI, then check three things: CI status, unresolved review threads, and whether the branch has fallen behind the base. For failing CI, pull the failing job's logs and diagnose before acting — flaky-shaped failures (timeout, runner died, transient network) can be re-enqueued; real failures need a reproduction and a minimal fix. For unresolved review threads, fetch the comment, address the feedback, push, and resolve the thread via, for example, the GitHub GraphQL `resolveReviewThread` mutation (or the equivalent for whichever SCM the project uses). Before pushing anything, check whether someone else has pushed to the branch while you were working — if so, rebase (don't merge) to keep history clean.

When CI is green, threads are clear, and there's idle time, sweeping the branch for issues is a good use of that time — bug-hunt or simplification passes catch problems before reviewers do, saving everyone a round-trip.

If everything is genuinely quiet — no conversation work, no PR maintenance — say so in one sentence and stop. No summary of what you checked, no list of what you might do later. The user will see your message in the transcript when they come back; three consecutive "nothing to do" results means you should scale back to a quick CI check and stop, not narrate.

## Repeated invocations

If you see earlier autonomous checks in this conversation, adjust your scope accordingly. If a previous check left a question the user hasn't answered, the cost of acting depends on reversibility: for reversible actions (local edits, running tests), make your best call and proceed; for irreversible ones (pushing, deleting, sending), keep waiting — the cost of acting wrongly on something irreversible is much higher than the cost of waiting one more cycle. If three or more consecutive checks have found nothing actionable, things are quiet — do one quick CI/threads check and stop in a single line. Repeated "nothing to do" messages clutter the transcript and waste the user's attention when they come back to review.

Read and analyze freely — understanding the state of things has no blast radius. Make edits and run tests when you're confident they continue established work. Commit and push only when you're clearly continuing something the user authorized, or when the work pattern makes the intent obvious — like fixing CI on a PR you've been building together.

import numpy as np
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.ndimage import gaussian_filter1d
from hera.analysis import fan_grids, resistance_grids, GateCalibration

fan = fan_grids("data/1")
ci = {c: i for i, c in enumerate(fan.cols)}
g = fan.data.reshape(fan.nrows, fan.nfast, len(fan.cols))
VTG = g[:, :, ci["DC_bias"]]          # (41,81) fast axis values
VBG = g[:, 0, ci["k_2400_volt"]]      # (41,)  slow axis values per row
tg_axis = VTG[0]                       # fast axis grid (same each row)
rg = resistance_grids(fan)

def extract_ridge(Rgrid):
    A = np.abs(Rgrid)
    As = gaussian_filter1d(A, sigma=1.5, axis=1)   # smooth along TG
    jpk = np.argmax(As, axis=1)
    vtg_cnp = tg_axis[jpk]
    rpk = A[np.arange(len(jpk)), jpk]
    edge = (jpk <= 1) | (jpk >= fan.nfast - 2)     # edge-clipped guard
    return vtg_cnp, rpk, jpk, edge

fits = {}
for ch in ("sr1", "sr2"):
    vtg_cnp, rpk, jpk, edge = extract_ridge(rg.R[ch])
    keep = ~edge
    # continuity guard: drop points >3*std from a first-pass linear fit
    c0 = np.polyfit(VBG[keep], vtg_cnp[keep], 1)
    resid = vtg_cnp - np.polyval(c0, VBG)
    good = keep & (np.abs(resid) < 3 * np.std(resid[keep]))
    slope, intc = np.polyfit(VBG[good], vtg_cnp[good], 1)
    rms = np.std(vtg_cnp[good] - np.polyval([slope, intc], VBG[good]))
    fits[ch] = dict(slope=slope, intc=intc, rms=rms, ngood=int(good.sum()),
                    nedge=int(edge.sum()), vtg_cnp=vtg_cnp, good=good, rpk=rpk)
    print(f"{ch}: slope dVtg/dVbg = {slope:+.4f}  -> c_bg/c_tg = {-slope:.4f} | "
          f"intercept(Vtg@Vbg=0) = {intc:+.4f} V | rms {rms*1e3:.1f} mV | "
          f"ngood {good.sum()}/{fan.nrows} (edge-clipped {edge.sum()})")

print(f"\ngeometry-prior ratio c_bg/c_tg = t_tg/t_bg = 15.6/12 = {15.6/12:.4f}")

# Cross-channel agreement
s1, s2 = fits["sr1"]["slope"], fits["sr2"]["slope"]
print(f"cross-channel slope agreement: {abs(s1-s2)/abs(0.5*(s1+s2))*100:.1f}% "
      f"(rms ~{0.5*(fits['sr1']['rms']+fits['sr2']['rms'])*1e3:.1f} mV)")

# Build calibration: anchor c_tg at geometry prior (t_tg=15.6nm); set ratio from fit (use sr1)
ratio = -fits["sr1"]["slope"]
t_tg = 15.6e-9
t_bg_eff = t_tg / ratio            # impose fitted ratio, keep c_tg absolute (geometry-prior scale)
cal = GateCalibration.from_thicknesses(t_tg, t_bg_eff, 0.0)
# n_offset so the fitted CNP line maps to n=0: at Vbg=0, Vtg_cnp = intercept
b = fits["sr1"]["intc"]
n0, d0 = cal.n_D(b, 0.0)
cal.n_offset = -n0
print(f"\nratio used (sr1) = {ratio:.4f} -> t_bg_eff = {t_bg_eff*1e9:.3f} nm")
print(f"n_offset set so CNP(Vtg={b:.3f},Vbg=0) -> n=0; raw n there was {n0:.3e} m^-2")

# Closure check: n along fitted ridge should be ~0
vtg_line = np.polyval([fits["sr1"]["slope"], fits["sr1"]["intc"]], VBG)
n_line, D_line = cal.n_D(vtg_line, VBG)
print(f"closure: |n| residual along fitted ridge max = {np.abs(n_line).max():.3e} m^-2 "
      f"({np.abs(n_line).max()/1e16:.3e} e12 cm^-2); D range {D_line.min():.3e}..{D_line.max():.3e} V/m")

# ---- plot: map (log|R|) + ridge + fit, per channel ----
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 5))
for ax, ch in zip(axes, ("sr1", "sr2")):
    A = np.abs(rg.R[ch])
    im = ax.pcolormesh(tg_axis, VBG, np.log10(A + 1), shading="nearest", cmap="viridis")
    f = fits[ch]
    ax.plot(f["vtg_cnp"][f["good"]], VBG[f["good"]], "r.", ms=5, label="CNP argmax")
    ax.plot(np.polyval([f["slope"], f["intc"]], VBG), VBG, "w--", lw=1.2,
            label=f"fit slope {f['slope']:+.3f}")
    ax.set_xlabel("V_tg (DC_bias) [V]"); ax.set_ylabel("V_bg [V]")
    ax.set_title(f"{ch}  log10|Rxx|  (run 1, B=0)"); ax.legend(loc="upper right", fontsize=8)
    fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax, label="log10(|R|+1)")
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig("hera_scratch/cnp_map.png", dpi=110)
print("saved hera_scratch/cnp_map.png")

# Device card — QC0426 (trilayer graphene)

*Session device card for QC0426 on the **VTI** cryostat. Deployed into the
measurement directory alongside the working notebooks. This card carries
**physical truth**: what is wired, the hardware, the outer safety box,
the provided gate operating limits, and the provided contact
configuration. The CNP location and (n, D) calibration are established
in-session (see the session brief).*

## Identity
- **Device id**: `QC0426`
- **Material**: trilayer graphene (`3LGr`).
- **Owner**: qingrui
- **Fridge**: VTI (variable-temperature insert). Base (sample)
  temperature ≈ 1.2–1.3 K.
- **Status**: cold, wired; no CNP location on record.

## Gate stack (three gates)
- **Top gate** (`k_tg`): hBN dielectric. **Driven by the SRS DC205** —
  in the data it appears as the column **`DC_bias`** (the
  DC205 voltage), and in sweep calls as `dc205_volt` (a
  `qcodes.Parameter` wrapping `k_tg.ramp_voltage`, `ramp_rate = 2`; the
  measure notebook's setup cells define it).
- **Back gate** (`k_bg`): thick graphite on hBN, driven by a **Keithley
  2400**.
- **Si global back gate** (`k_si` / `k_2410`): doped-Si gate through
  **SiO₂**, driven by a second Keithley (`k_2410`). The graphite back gate
  screens Si from the channel — Si couples only to the contacts
  (contact-doping gate). Operating limit provided (below).
- **Gate-stack geometry** (fabrication facts; **geometry prior only** —
  the capacitance *calibration* is the session's to establish via
  `cnp-and-dline-calibration`):
  ```python
  from sharpelab_nb.gates import stack_capacitance, calc_nD, calc_gate_voltages
  c_tg = stack_capacitance([(15.6, 3)])           # 15.6 nm hBN
  c_bg = stack_capacitance([(12, 3), (0, 3.9)])   # 12 nm hBN, no SiO2 term
  ```
  Treat anything derived from these (lever arms, n/D scales, CNP-line
  slope) as uncalibrated until the session's own gate map confirms it.

## Gate operating limits — gate B contract

Gate operating limits for the session:

| Parameter | Operating limit | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `dc205_volt` / `k_tg` | **[−6.0, +7.0] V** | provided; geometry ceiling is the hard fence behind it |
| `k_bg.volt` | **[−4.5, +4.5] V** | provided |
| `k_2410.volt` (Si) | **[−50, +50] V** | provided |
| **B field (session cap)** | **\|B\| ≤ 8.0 T** | committed on the `magnet.field` validator (SAFETIES); driver `max_field_T = 14.0` T is the hard backstop |

## Measurement setup (rig instruments wired this cooldown)
- **Gates**: top via **DC205** (`DC_bias`), back via **k_bg** Keithley,
  Si via **k_2410** Keithley.
- **AC excitation / lock-ins**: SR830 family (`sr0…sr3` live).
  Current-bias drive: **0.5 V through a 100 MΩ bias resistor**, lock-in
  frequency **≈ 13 Hz**.
- **Current channel**: **`sr0`** = drain current, **`sr0_gain = −1E6`**
  (Ithaco preamp gain). Per-channel sensitivities are recorded per run in
  `measurement_config`.
- **Lock-in time constant**: 0.3 s, 24 dB/oct, all channels (`sr0`–`sr3`).
  Minimum dwell 4·τ = 1.2 s/pt.
- **Sensitivity by signal scale**: CNP / gate-map (kΩ) ~2e-5 on the voltage
  channels; high-|n| metallic (tens of Ω) `sr1` 2e-6, `sr2` 5e-7, `sr3` 5e-6,
  `sr0` 1e-2.
- **Bias current**: 0.5 V / 5 nA through the 100 MΩ default; high-|n| metallic
  regime ~2 V / 20 nA.
- **Voltage channels**: `sr1, sr2, sr3` carry four-terminal voltages.
  `sr3` is the Hall channel (`r_xy`).
- **Contact switching — QSwitch (QDevil) mux** — ContactMux live:
  - Wiring topology (final per the operator's
    routing slide): device pads bond to two Fischer cables; the
    QSwitch takes **F1 only**, and F2-riding contact pads are shorted
    onto spare F1 conductors at the breakout. **F1 fischer index =
    QSwitch line number.** TG and BG do **not** pass through the
    QSwitch (hardwired to their sources — fixed, unswitchable). Si
    passes through the QSwitch and back to the breakout box.
  - **Contact map** (label = position, T = top arc L→R, B = left side
    then bottom L→R; all switchable):

    | Label | Pad | Line | | Label | Pad | Line |
    |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
    | T1 | F2-05 | 1 | | B1 | F2-37 | 8 |
    | T2 | F1-33 | 3 | | B2 | F2-21 | 17 |
    | T3 | F1-09 | 4 | | B3 | F1-28 | 23 |
    | T4 | F1-01 | 6 | | B4 | F1-12 | 22 |
    | T5 | F1-42 | 7 | | B5 | F1-20 | 20 |
    | T6 | F1-02 | 12 | | B6 | F1-44 | 19 |
    | T7 | F1-43 | 13 | | B7 | F1-03 | 18 |
    | | | | | B8 | F1-35 | 15 |

    Alive: T2, T3, T4, T5, B3, B4, B5, B6, B7. Dead: T1, T6, T7, B1, B8
    (B2 high-R).

  - **Gates**: TG (DC205) and BG (K2400) **hardwired — no relay can
    touch them**. **Si (K2410) rides QSwitch lines 16 and 11** with
    standing closed relays ("keep 16/11 closed inside the QSwitch" —
    routed through the switch and back to the breakout box). Lines
    16/11 are **excluded from ContactMux's managed set** (never in the
    `lines` map), and **`qsw.reset()` is always forbidden** — it opens
    the standing closures and drops the Si gate.
  - **Instrument taps (BNC 1–8)**: 1 = sr1.V1, 2 = sr1.V2, 3 = sr2.V1,
    4 = sr2.V2, 5 = sr3.V1, 6 = sr3.V2, **7 = sr1.amplitude (AC
    source)**, **8 = sr0.V1 × −1e6 (measured AC current)**. ContactMux
    form: `breakouts = {"source": 7, "drain": 8, "sr1+": 1, "sr1-": 2,
    "sr2+": 3, "sr2-": 4, "sr3+": 5, "sr3-": 6}`.
  - `settle_s` **4 s**.
- **Provided contact configuration**:

  | role | label | QSwitch line |
  |---|---|---|
  | source | T2 | 3 |
  | drain (`sr0`) | B7 | 18 |
  | `sr1` (Rxx) | T3–T4 | 4, 6 |
  | `sr2` (Rxx) | B4–B5 | 22, 20 |
  | `sr3` (Rxy, Hall) | T5–B6 | 7, 19 |

  "T3", "sr1-": "T4", "sr2+": "B4", "sr2-": "B5", "sr3+": "T5", "sr3-":

6	onset field and the tone frequencies — by FFT in 1/B. Mechanically this is a
7	`field-sweep-1d` (see it for the Station / sweep / fp / plot call surface); what
8	makes it a *spot check* is the design discipline below — the field range, 1/B spacing
9	Δ(1/B), and settling are chosen to resolve the tones cleanly, and the read is the 1/B
10	FFT.
11	It is the cheap 1D precursor to a `landau-fan`: one density, but **full per-point
12	quality**.
13	
14	## When
15	- **Before committing a `landau-fan`.** A spot check pins the **onset** (sets the
16	  fan's B-range), the **observed tone frequencies** (confirm/correct the fan's
17	  Δ(1/B)), and the **settling/sensitivity** the fan inherits. A fan is the dense
18	  version; a couple of clean spot checks de-risk it — and can answer the question
19	  outright (`investigations/trilayer-stacking-fs-count.md` Step 3).
20	- Whenever a `field-sweep-1d` or `gatemap` showed QO-like wiggles and you want the
21	  frequency content at a point, not the whole (n, B) plane.
22	
23	## Why
24	A spot check is cheap because it is **one density (1D), not because it is
25	low-quality**. Its whole value is being acquired *well* — at the settling floor and
26	Nyquist on the fastest tone — so a clean spot check can be decisive on its own and a
27	noisier fan cannot overturn it (`landau-fan`). Two knobs carry the quality:
28	
29	- **Sampling.** The fastest tone sets the finest 1/B period. The reference frequency
30	  **F_L = (h/g·e)·n** (g = 4) — what a single four-fold pocket carrying all the
31	  density would give — is an upper bound on the fastest tone; Nyquist it. Undersampling
32	  the fast tone folds its aliases into the low-frequency band, where they masquerade
33	  as a small/slow tone (Verify).
34	- **Settling.** A swept-point dwell has a floor near the lock-in time constant
35	  (dwell ≥ k·τ; k ≈ 5 at 6 dB/oct, 7–10 at 24 dB/oct). Under-settling **attenuates
36	  the oscillation amplitude itself** (the filter cannot track the QO) — benign on a
37	  smooth slope, but it *buries a small tone* (Verify). The floor is non-negotiable
38	  when the target is a weak tone.
39	
40	## Recipe
41	1. **Density + range.** Pick the density — high |n| gives the most periods and the
42	   clearest tones. Sweep a field window **[B_lo, B_hi]** sampled **uniformly in 1/B**
43	   (`field_invB`), not in B: SdH oscillations are periodic in 1/B, so even spacing there
44	   gives constant points-per-period and FFTs the raw points (no resample). `B_lo` is a
45	   small positive floor (~0.1–0.3 T) below the expected **onset** — uniform-1/B is
46	   densest in B at low field, so it captures the onset (the lowest B where oscillations
47	   emerge once the MR background is subtracted) for free.
48	2. **Δ(1/B) from F_L.** Compute F_L = (h/4e)·n and Nyquist-resolve it: Δ(1/B) ≤ 1/(2·F_L)
49	   (prefer 1/3). Set N from the window: N = (1/B_lo − 1/B_hi)/Δ(1/B) + 1. This Δ(1/B)
50	   (and N) is what a committed fan inherits.
51	3. **Lock-in.** Set sensitivity so full scale ≈ I_bias × R_target — a signal at a
52	   few % of range is coarse-ADC digitized (the grainy-FFT failure). Set the dwell at
53	   the settling floor (Why); read τ and the filter slope, do not guess them.

55	   build the Station, ramp the gates to (n, D), `s.sweep(mag.field,
56	   field_invB(B_start, B_end, N), delay=dwell)`, fp the temperature(s) and every

quality**.

low-quality**. Its whole value is being acquired *well* — at the settling floor and

  density would give — is an upper bound on the fastest tone; Nyquist it. Undersampling

  as a small/slow tone (Verify).

  (dwell ≥ k·τ; k ≈ 5 at 6 dB/oct, 7–10 at 24 dB/oct). Under-settling **attenuates

   emerge once the MR background is subtracted) for free.

   (prefer 1/3). Set N from the window: N = (1/B_lo − 1/B_hi)/Δ(1/B) + 1. This Δ(1/B)
   (and N) is what a committed fan inherits.

   few % of range is coarse-ADC digitized (the grainy-FFT failure). Set the dwell at
   the settling floor (Why); read τ and the filter slope, do not guess them.

   lock-in X/P, plot the live MR and gate-current leakage.

   - **Onset** — `hera.analysis.sdh_onset(R, B)` returns an `SdhOnset`: `onset_b` and

from hera.analysis import fan_grids, resistance_grids, GateCalibration

import numpy as np
import time
import scipy.constants as cst

# Target: HOLE side, n = -3.5e12 cm^-2, D = 0 (session calibration, run 1)
VTG_T, VBG_T = -1.5597, -1.1914     # gates_for(-3.5e12, 0); n, D verified exact
n_target = 3.5e16                    # m^-2
F_L = cst.h / (4 * cst.e) * n_target # g=4 Luttinger freq (T)
B_LO, B_HI = 0.20, 7.95
dinvB = 1.0 / (3 * F_L)              # Nyquist/3 on F_L
N = int(np.ceil((1 / B_LO - 1 / B_HI) / dinvB)) + 1
Bvec = 1.0 / np.linspace(1 / B_LO, 1 / B_HI, N)   # uniform in 1/B, 0.20 -> 7.95 T
print(f"F_L={F_L:.1f} T  d(1/B)={dinvB:.2e}  N={N}  Bvec {Bvec[0]:.3f}..{Bvec[-1]:.3f} T")

# Lock-in sensitivities for high-|n| metallic SdH (NOT touching tau/filter_slope)
sr1.sensitivity(1e-5); sr2.sensitivity(1e-5); sr3.sensitivity(5e-5)

meas_config['comments'] = (f"sdh-spot-check HOLE n=-3.5e12 D=0 (Vtg={VTG_T},Vbg={VBG_T}); "
                           f"B {B_LO}->{B_HI}T uniform-1/B N={N} (Nyquist/3 F_L={F_L:.1f}T); "
                           f"dwell 2.5s (8tau@24dB); sr1/2=1e-5 sr3=5e-5; Si=0.")
for k, sr in [('sr0_sens', sr0), ('sr1_sens', sr1), ('sr2_sens', sr2), ('sr3_sens', sr3)]:
    meas_config[k] = sr.sensitivity()
meas_config['bias_voltage'] = sr1.amplitude(); meas_config['lockin_freq'] = sr1.frequency()
meas_config['sample_temperature:'] = heater.sample_temperature(); meas_config['Si (V)'] = k_si.volt()

# Preflight
print("T:", heater.sample_temperature(), "K  B:", magnet.field(), "T  Si:", k_si.volt(),
      "V  drive:", sr1.amplitude(), "V  sens(1/2/3):", sr1.sensitivity(), sr2.sensitivity(), sr3.sensitivity())

# Ramp gates to (n, D=0), then magnet to B_lo (blocks until reached)
dc205_volt(VTG_T); k_bg.volt(VBG_T); time.sleep(3)
magnet.field(B_LO)
print("at start B =", magnet.field(), "T")

s = async_station(meas_config)
s.add_comment('sdh-spot-check')
s.add_comment(f'HOLE n=-3.5e12 D=0 B{B_LO}-{B_HI}T invB N{N} dwell2.5')
s.fp(sr0.X).fp(sr0.P).fp(sr1.X).fp(sr1.P).fp(sr2.X).fp(sr2.P).fp(sr3.X).fp(sr3.P)
s.fp(k_bg.curr).fp(k_si.curr)
s.plot(magnet.field, sr1.X)
s.sweep(magnet.field, Bvec, delay=2.5)
print("spot check complete; B now", magnet.field(), "T")

import numpy as np
import matplotlib; matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from hera.analysis import open_run, sdh_onset, sdh_fft
import scipy.constants as cst

r = open_run("data/2")
B = r.col("magnet_field")
i = r.col("sr0_X") / (-1e6)
R1 = r.col("sr1_X") / i
R2 = r.col("sr2_X") / i
print(f"rows {len(B)}, B {B.min():.3f}..{B.max():.3f} T")
print(f"Rxx sr1 {R1.min():.0f}..{R1.max():.0f} ohm ; sr2 {R2.min():.0f}..{R2.max():.0f} ohm")
# overload check: V = R*I vs FS (sr1/2 1e-5=10uV)
Vmax1 = (np.abs(R1)*np.abs(i)).max()*1e6
print(f"max |V| sr1 = {Vmax1:.2f} uV (FS=10uV) -> {'OK' if Vmax1<10 else 'CLIPPED'}")

n = 3.5e16; F_L = cst.h/(4*cst.e)*n
print(f"F_L = {F_L:.1f} T")

# Onset on sr1
try:
    on = sdh_onset(R1, B)
    print(f"onset_b={on.onset_b:.3f} T  clip_high_b={on.clip_high_b:.3f} T  consensus_freq={on.consensus_freq:.1f} T")
    cutoff = on.onset_b
except Exception as e:
    print("onset failed:", e); cutoff = 1.5

fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(16, 4.5))
ax[0].plot(B, R1, lw=0.7, label="sr1"); ax[0].plot(B, R2, lw=0.7, label="sr2")
ax[0].set_xlabel("B [T]"); ax[0].set_ylabel("Rxx [ohm]"); ax[0].legend(); ax[0].set_title("Rxx(B) PARTIAL")
# bg-subtracted vs 1/B
for ch, R, c in [("sr1", R1, "C0"), ("sr2", R2, "C1")]:
    m = B >= max(cutoff, 1.0)
    coef = np.polyfit(B[m], R[m], 5); dR = R[m] - np.polyval(coef, B[m])
    ax[1].plot(1/B[m], dR, lw=0.7, color=c, label=ch)
ax[1].set_xlabel("1/B [1/T]"); ax[1].set_ylabel("dRxx [ohm]"); ax[1].legend(); ax[1].set_title(f"bg-sub (B>{max(cutoff,1.0):.1f}T)")
# FFT
for ch, R, c in [("sr1", R1, "C0"), ("sr2", R2, "C1")]:
    f, mag = sdh_fft(R, B, b_range=(max(cutoff, 1.0), B.max()), bg_degree=5)
    ax[2].plot(f, mag, color=c, label=ch)
ax[2].axvline(F_L, ls="--", c="k", lw=1, label=f"F_L={F_L:.0f}T")
ax[2].set_xlabel("F [T]"); ax[2].set_ylabel("FFT mag"); ax[2].set_xlim(0, 1.3*F_L)
ax[2].legend(); ax[2].set_title("SdH FFT PARTIAL")
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig("hera_scratch/sc1_partial.png", dpi=110)
print("saved hera_scratch/sc1_partial.png")

B = r.col("magnet_field")

R1 = r.col("sr1_X") / i

print(f"rows {len(B)}, B {B.min():.3f}..{B.max():.3f} T")
print(f"Rxx sr1 {R1.min():.0f}..{R1.max():.0f} ohm ; sr2 {R2.min():.0f}..{R2.max():.0f} ohm")
# overload check: V = R*I vs FS (sr1/2 1e-5=10uV)
Vmax1 = (np.abs(R1)*np.abs(i)).max()*1e6

n = 3.5e16; F_L = cst.h/(4*cst.e)*n

try:

    cutoff = on.onset_b
except Exception as e:
    print("onset failed:", e); cutoff = 1.5

fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(16, 4.5))
ax[0].plot(B, R1, lw=0.7, label="sr1"); ax[0].plot(B, R2, lw=0.7, label="sr2")
ax[0].set_xlabel("B [T]"); ax[0].set_ylabel("Rxx [ohm]"); ax[0].legend(); ax[0].set_title("Rxx(B) PARTIAL")

import numpy as np
import matplotlib; matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from hera.analysis import open_run, sdh_fft
import scipy.constants as cst

r = open_run("data/3")
B = r.col("magnet_field"); i = r.col("sr0_X") / (-1e6)
R1 = r.col("sr1_X") / i; R2 = r.col("sr2_X") / i
order = np.argsort(B); B, R1, R2 = B[order], R1[order], R2[order]
n = 3.5e16; F_L = cst.h / (4 * cst.e) * n
print(f"F_L={F_L:.1f} T ; B {B.min():.2f}-{B.max():.2f} T ; {len(B)} pts")

fig, ax = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(14, 9))
# (0,0) raw Rxx(B)
ax[0,0].plot(B, R1, ".-", ms=3, lw=0.7, label="sr1 T3-T4")
ax[0,0].plot(B, R2, ".-", ms=3, lw=0.7, label="sr2 B4-B5")
ax[0,0].set_xlabel("B [T]"); ax[0,0].set_ylabel("Rxx [ohm]"); ax[0,0].legend()
ax[0,0].set_title("Run 3 raw Rxx(B) HOLE n=-3.5e12 (clean sens)")

# (0,1) bg-subtracted vs 1/B (poly deg-5 in B), cutoff 1.5T
cutoff = 1.5
for ch, R, c in [("sr1", R1, "C0"), ("sr2", R2, "C1")]:
    m = B >= cutoff
    coef = np.polyfit(B[m], R[m], 5); dR = R[m] - np.polyval(coef, B[m])
    ax[0,1].plot(1/B[m], dR, ".-", ms=3, lw=0.7, color=c, label=ch)
ax[0,1].set_xlabel("1/B [1/T]"); ax[0,1].set_ylabel("dRxx [ohm]")
ax[0,1].legend(); ax[0,1].set_title(f"bg-subtracted (B>={cutoff}T) vs 1/B")

# (1,0) FFT at several cutoffs (sr1)
for cut, c in [(1.0, "C0"), (1.5, "C1"), (2.5, "C2"), (3.5, "C3")]:
    f, mag = sdh_fft(R1, B, b_range=(cut, B.max()), bg_degree=5)
    ax[1,0].plot(f, mag, color=c, lw=1, label=f"sr1 cut {cut}T")
ax[1,0].axvline(F_L, ls="--", c="k", lw=1.2, label=f"F_L={F_L:.0f}T")
ax[1,0].set_xlabel("F [T]"); ax[1,0].set_ylabel("FFT mag"); ax[1,0].set_xlim(0, 1.3*F_L)
ax[1,0].legend(fontsize=8); ax[1,0].set_title("sr1 FFT vs cutoff (stability)")

# (1,1) FFT sr1 vs sr2 at cutoff 1.5
for ch, R, c in [("sr1", R1, "C0"), ("sr2", R2, "C1")]:
    f, mag = sdh_fft(R, B, b_range=(1.5, B.max()), bg_degree=5)
    ax[1,1].plot(f, mag, color=c, lw=1.2, label=ch)
    pk = f[1:][np.argmax(mag[1:])]
    print(f"{ch}: dominant FFT peak at F={pk:.1f} T  (F_L={F_L:.1f}); F_L/peak={F_L/pk:.2f}")
ax[1,1].axvline(F_L, ls="--", c="k", lw=1.2, label=f"F_L={F_L:.0f}T")
ax[1,1].set_xlabel("F [T]"); ax[1,1].set_ylabel("FFT mag"); ax[1,1].set_xlim(0, 1.3*F_L)
ax[1,1].legend(fontsize=8); ax[1,1].set_title("FFT sr1 vs sr2 (cut 1.5T)")
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig("hera_scratch/sc1b_fft.png", dpi=110)
print("saved hera_scratch/sc1b_fft.png")

N = int(np.ceil((1 / B_LO - 1 / B_HI) / dinvB)) + 1

**Read:** HOLE side, n=−3.5×10¹², base T — **resolution-limited, no FS count extractable (a fork, not a number).**

- **Onset is high** (~3 T; sdh_onset returns nan/1.1 T inconsistently): no clean oscillations below ~3 T. Consistent with the warm electron-T (~8 K) — the SdH amplitude is thermally suppressed at low B, so oscillations only emerge at high field.
- **Short 1/B record → coarse resolution.** Usable window ~3–8 T → 1/B span ~0.21, δf ~ 5 T (best ~2.7 T extending to 2 T). The high-field oscillations are large (±50–100 Ω) but **few and irregular** — not the many clean periods a sharp FFT needs.
- **FFT peak wanders across extraction choices** — 4 T / 36 T / 19 T / 24 T as cutoff goes 1.5→4 T, and 10→19 T as bg-degree goes 3→7. The low-F (~4 T) content is residual MR-background (degree-poly can't fully remove the strong B^1.8 MR); the "blob" sits ~10–20 T with no sharp, stable line, and little power at F_L=36 T. **By STYLE rule 14 this is a fork to report, not a frequency to refine.**
- **No robust tone, no Luttinger partition** can be claimed here. This does **not** distinguish ABA (pair summing to F_L) from ABC (single tone at F_L) — both are unresolved at this T/record-length.

**Implication:** the hole side at this density is a resolution-limited cannot-tell. Next: the electron-side mirror (run 4, in flight) tests whether the other side is cleaner; if both are limited, the read pivots to the **Step-6 high-field Streda/Chern offset** (bigger gaps, resolvable at warm T) or a resolution-limited cannot-tell with the onset/mobility number — a device-quality/rig statement, not more low-field fans. The Step-4 fan is **not** yet justified (a fan inherits the spot check's acquisition; a fan here would be equally resolution-limited).

import scipy.constants as cst

r = open_run("data/4")
B = r.col("magnet_field"); i = r.col("sr0_X") / (-1e6)
R1 = r.col("sr1_X") / i; R2 = r.col("sr2_X") / i
o = np.argsort(B); B, R1, R2 = B[o], R1[o], R2[o]
F_L = cst.h / (4 * cst.e) * 3.5e16
print(f"F_L={F_L:.1f} T")

fig, ax = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(14, 9))
ax[0,0].plot(B, R1, ".-", ms=3, lw=0.7, label="sr1 T3-T4")
ax[0,0].plot(B, R2, ".-", ms=3, lw=0.7, label="sr2 B4-B5")
ax[0,0].set_xlabel("B [T]"); ax[0,0].set_ylabel("Rxx [ohm]"); ax[0,0].legend()
ax[0,0].set_title("Run 4 raw Rxx(B) ELECTRON n=+3.5e12 D=0 (clean)")

# bg-sub vs 1/B (count periods)
for ch, R, c in [("sr1", R1, "C0"), ("sr2", R2, "C1")]:
    m = B >= 1.5
    coef = np.polyfit(B[m], R[m], 4); dR = R[m] - np.polyval(coef, B[m])
    ax[0,1].plot(1/B[m], dR, ".-", ms=3, lw=0.8, color=c, label=ch)
ax[0,1].set_xlabel("1/B [1/T]"); ax[0,1].set_ylabel("dRxx [ohm]"); ax[0,1].legend()
ax[0,1].set_title("bg-sub vs 1/B (B>1.5T) — clean periodic?"); ax[0,1].grid(alpha=0.3)

# FFT both channels, several cutoffs (sr1)
for cut, c in [(1.5, "C0"), (2.0, "C1"), (3.0, "C2")]:
    f, mag = sdh_fft(R1[:, None], B, b_range=(cut, B.max()), bg_degree=5)
    mag = np.asarray(mag).squeeze(); ax[1,0].plot(f, mag/mag[f>2].max(), lw=1, label=f"sr1 cut {cut}T")
ax[1,0].axvline(F_L, ls="--", c="k", lw=1.2, label=f"F_L={F_L:.0f}T")
ax[1,0].set_xlabel("F [T]"); ax[1,0].set_ylabel("norm FFT"); ax[1,0].set_xlim(0, 60)
ax[1,0].legend(fontsize=8); ax[1,0].set_title("sr1 FFT vs cutoff (stable peak?)")

# sr1 vs sr2 at cut 2T, search secondary peaks
from scipy.signal import find_peaks
for ch, R, c in [("sr1", R1, "C0"), ("sr2", R2, "C1")]:
    f, mag = sdh_fft(R[:, None], B, b_range=(2.0, B.max()), bg_degree=5)
    mag = np.asarray(mag).squeeze(); magn = mag/mag[f>2].max()

    pk, props = find_peaks(magn[(f>3)], height=0.15)

for cut in (1.5, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0):

        pks.append(f[f > 2][np.argmax(m[f > 2])])
    print(f"  cut {cut:.1f}T  bg(3,5,7): " + ", ".join(f"{p:5.1f}T" for p in pks))

fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 4.5))
for cut, c in [(1.5, "C0"), (2.0, "C1"), (3.0, "C2")]:
    f, m = sdh_fft(R1[:, None], B, b_range=(cut, B.max()), bg_degree=5); m = np.asarray(m).squeeze()

The smaller satellite peaks (~6, 14, 21, 30, 40, 50 T, spaced ~6 T) are consistent with **sidelobe ringing** of one strong tone in a short 1/B record, not a resolved second pocket. An ABA reading (f_BL ≈ 34 T with a small, unresolved f_ML ≈ F_L − f_BL ≈ 2 T) **cannot be excluded** at this single density / resolution — that's the known ABA-vs-ABC ambiguity (ABA's f_BL nearly coincides with ABC's single tone).

# Session notes — QC0426 / vti

Operational log (not a science notebook).

## E1 grant — 2026-06-21
Operator (Zack) granted autonomy: "Ramp down is appropriate. go for autonomy"
once Gate A + Gate B were green and bring-up VERIFY flags addressed. E1 engaged.
First E1 execute = read-only kernel-binding probe (per VERIFY); then magnet
ramp 0.30 T -> 0 T; then Gate C contact liveness -> Step 1 (B=0 gate map / CNP).

## TOOLING — gatemap recipe is toploader-API; no gatemap-vti variant (2026-06-21)
`measurements/gatemap.md` is written in toploader API (`k_tg.volt`, `s.AsyncStation`,
fp temperature). Adapted to VTI for run 0 (Gate C) and the Step-1 map: TG axis =
`dc205_volt` (data col `DC_bias`), set-only param; no TG current monitor so gate
leakage is watched only on `k_bg.curr`/`k_si.curr`; temperature is NOT fp'd
per-point (rig card: LS335 Grafana co-master, per-point poll has killed a run) —
T captured once in `meas_config`. Station built via `async_station(meas_config)`.
A `gatemap-vti` variant capturing these deltas would help.

## PROTOCOL — settling floor vs bring-up dwell (2026-06-21)
Lock-ins read 24 dB/oct, tau=0.3 s (all channels). Rig-card settling floor at
24 dB/oct is k~7-10 tau = 2.1-3 s; the bring-up/Gate C dwell of 4 tau = 1.2 s is
BELOW it, so features can be mildly smeared (small notch at V_bg=0 in run 0).
Reasoning used for Step-1 map: a *constant* fast-axis settling lag shifts the CNP
ridge by the same amount in every row -> biases the intercept (offset) only, NOT
the slope (cap ratio). So the calibration map runs at fast_delay~1.0 s safely for
the ratio; SdH spot-checks/fan will lock proper settling per investigation Step 3.
Did not change filter_slope (operator-owned front-panel setting per rig card).

## FEEDBACK/data — Gate C result (run 0, 2026-06-21)
CNP at TG=0 is V_bg = +0.40 V, peak Rxx ~1.9 kOhm on BOTH sr1(T3-T4) & sr2(B4-B5)
(agree). Geometry-prior cap ratio c_bg/c_tg = t_tg/t_bg = 15.6/12 = 1.30 -> expected
CNP line V_tg ~= -1.30*V_bg + 0.52. Gate leakage at Keithley 1uA-range noise floor
(|I_bg|<=0.24 nA, |I_si|<=0.58 nA), not genuine. Contacts alive.

## Step 1 DONE — (n,D) calibration (run 1, 2026-06-21/22)
B=0 gate map (41x81, 74 min) -> cap ratio c_bg/c_tg = 1.309 (sr1)/1.300 (sr2),

content.content:
# Trilayer FS-count forward model — ABA vs ABC

Backs the `recipes/investigations/trilayer-stacking-fs-count.md` investigation.
Where `models/aba_trilayer/` computes the **Landau-fan crossing structure** (the
Datta fingerprint), this model computes the **B = 0 Fermi-surface count** and the
**Onsager frequencies** the FS-count read overlays on data: ABA ≥ 2 coexisting
surfaces (ML Dirac + BL parabolic) vs ABC's single post-Lifshitz pocket.

The survey that grounds it (band structure, the three ingested papers, the
feasibility numbers) is `docs/stacking-extraction-survey.md`; read it for the
physics. This README covers what the tools are and how to run them.

## Files

| File | What it does |
|---|---|
| `fs_count_b0.py` | B = 0 FS count + Onsager F(n, D). **ABA** from the continuum 6-site SWMcC Hamiltonian (Datta params, γ₃=γ₄=0 — same parameters as `models/aba_trilayer/ll_spectrum.py`); **ABC** from the MacDonald PRB 82, 035409 (2010) effective two-band model (Eq. 6/7) with trigonal warping → the 3-pocket → annulus → single-pocket Lifshitz cascade. Counts distinct extremal-orbit frequencies F = (ℏ/2πe)·A_k. Pure numpy/scipy. |
| `plots.py` | Renders `{aba_bands_linecut, abc_bands_linecut, abc_bands_contour, luttinger_vs_n}.png` from `fs_count_b0`. |
| `ll_sequence.py` | High-field complement: ABA Landau-level fan + QH/Streda sequence (the pseudo-decoupled ML Dirac band offsets the Chern sequence; non-dispersing ML N=0 doublet). Imports the validated `models/aba_trilayer/ll_spectrum.py`. Outputs `aba_LL_fan.png`, `aba_wannier.png`. |
| `*.png` | Generated figures (band linecuts, ABC contour, Luttinger-sum check, LL fan, Wannier diagram). |
| `rmg-fft-snapshot/` | Frozen copy of the RMG SdH-FFT analysis pipeline (background-subtract in B → interp to 1/B → window → FFT, with the stability-sweep hygiene). A **reference snapshot, not a standalone package** — see its `PROVENANCE.md`; reconcile into `hera.analysis.sdh_fft` later. |

## Run

```bash
cd hera/models/trilayer_fs_count
uv run --no-project --with numpy --with scipy python3 fs_count_b0.py              # FS count + Onsager frequencies
uv run --no-project --with numpy --with scipy --with matplotlib python3 plots.py # band/Luttinger figures
uv run --no-project --with numpy --with scipy --with matplotlib python3 ll_sequence.py  # high-field Streda fan
```
(`--no-project` pulls just numpy/scipy/matplotlib — the worktree's submodules
aren't checked out, so `uv sync` can't run here.)

## Validation

- **Luttinger sum** Σf = n at the right degeneracy reproduces in both models at
  every density tested — the model-independent consistency check on the count.
- `fs_count_b0` reproduces MacDonald's trigonal-warping Lifshitz cascade location
  (~10¹¹ cm⁻²), so ABC presents a single Fermi surface at the ~10¹² operating
  density.
- `ll_sequence` builds on the already-validated `aba_trilayer/ll_spectrum.py`
  (the 2 meV / 14 meV band splittings gate that model).

## Gap / future work

A quantitative **ABC** Landau-level model is **not yet built** — only ABA is
computed, so the high-field Streda/Chern contrast (recipe Step 6) is qualitative
on the ABC side. See `docs/stacking-extraction-survey.md` §9. A candidate
implementation to adapt is Dan Parker's `RhombohedralGrapheneLandau.jl`, though
it appears R4G (tetralayer)-specific and would need trilayer adaptation.

**Onsager F(n) is numerically clamped above |n| ≈ 3.5e12 cm⁻²** (`aba_fs` E_F
search capped at 70 meV; `abc_fs` a 50 meV window + `kmax`): above the density
the energy/k grid reaches, `np.interp` clamps to the grid edge instead of
failing, so F(n) **flattens spuriously**. This is a solver-domain artifact, *not*
a model-validity limit. Consequence: the curves do not reach the QC0426 operating
density (±8e12), so the Step-5 overlay cannot currently be run at the operating
point. **TODO (Aaron + Claude to revisit):** extend the grids to cover the
operating range, and/or make the solver raise/NaN above its covered range rather
than silently clamp.

fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig("hera_scratch/fan_verdict.png", dpi=110)
print("saved hera_scratch/fan_verdict.png")

# Luttinger / partition diagnostic per column

for j in range(len(n_vec)):

    f, mag = sdh_fft(R[oB, :], Bs5, b_range=(cutoff, Bs5.max()), bg_degree=5); mag = np.asarray(mag)
    return np.array([f[f > fmin][np.argmax(mag[j, f > fmin])] for j in range(mag.shape[0])])
F1 = fpk(R1f); F2 = fpk(R2f)

ns = np.linspace(1.5e16, 3.5e16, 16); aba_lo, aba_hi, abc_f = [], [], []
for n in ns:
    _, fs = fsc.aba_fs(n); Fs = sorted(F for F, k in fs)
    aba_lo.append(Fs[0]); aba_hi.append(Fs[-1]); abc_f.append(fsc.abc_fs(n)[4])
aba_lo, aba_hi, abc_f = map(np.array, (aba_lo, aba_hi, abc_f))
m = n_col >= 1.5e16
lams = np.linspace(0.8, 1.2, 41)
lam = lams[np.argmin([np.nanmean((F1[m] - np.interp(l * n_col[m], ns, abc_f))**2) for l in lams])]
print(f"ABA(ML,BL)@2.5e12=({np.interp(2.5e16,ns,aba_lo):.1f},{np.interp(2.5e16,ns,aba_hi):.1f})T ; "
      f"ABC@2.5e12={np.interp(2.5e16,ns,abc_f):.1f}T ; global rescale lambda={lam:.3f}")

plt.figure(figsize=(8, 5.5))
plt.plot(ns/1e16, abc_f, "g-", lw=2, label="ABC single pocket")
plt.plot(ns/1e16, aba_hi, "b-", lw=1.5, label="ABA BL")
plt.plot(ns/1e16, aba_lo, "b--", lw=1.5, label="ABA ML (discriminator)")
plt.plot(n_col/1e16, F_Lc, "k:", lw=0.8, label="F_L")
plt.plot(n_col[m]/1e16, F1[m], "o", color="C3", ms=5, label="sr1 measured")
plt.plot(n_col[m]/1e16, F2[m], "s", color="C1", ms=4, label="sr2 measured")
plt.xlabel("n [10^12 cm^-2]"); plt.ylabel("F [T]"); plt.legend(fontsize=8)
plt.title(f"FS-count: F(n) vs Onsager model (rescale lambda={lam:.2f})")
plt.ylim(0, 40); plt.show()
print("KEY: ABA-BL ~ ABC ~ F_L (coincide); the only discriminator (ABA-ML) sits <~2T,")
print("below this run's resolution (df~1.9T) and in the MR-background band.")

Operational log (not a science notebook).

## E1 grant — 2026-06-21
Operator (Zack) granted autonomy: "Ramp down is appropriate. go for autonomy"
once Gate A + Gate B were green and bring-up VERIFY flags addressed. E1 engaged.
First E1 execute = read-only kernel-binding probe (per VERIFY); then magnet

## TOOLING — gatemap recipe is toploader-API; no gatemap-vti variant (2026-06-21)
`measurements/gatemap.md` is written in toploader API (`k_tg.volt`, `s.AsyncStation`,
fp temperature). Adapted to VTI for run 0 (Gate C) and the Step-1 map: TG axis =
`dc205_volt` (data col `DC_bias`), set-only param; no TG current monitor so gate
leakage is watched only on `k_bg.curr`/`k_si.curr`; temperature is NOT fp'd
per-point (rig card: LS335 Grafana co-master, per-point poll has killed a run) —

A `gatemap-vti` variant capturing these deltas would help.

## PROTOCOL — settling floor vs bring-up dwell (2026-06-21)
Lock-ins read 24 dB/oct, tau=0.3 s (all channels). Rig-card settling floor at
24 dB/oct is k~7-10 tau = 2.1-3 s; the bring-up/Gate C dwell of 4 tau = 1.2 s is
BELOW it, so features can be mildly smeared (small notch at V_bg=0 in run 0).
Reasoning used for Step-1 map: a *constant* fast-axis settling lag shifts the CNP
ridge by the same amount in every row -> biases the intercept (offset) only, NOT
the slope (cap ratio). So the calibration map runs at fast_delay~1.0 s safely for
the ratio; SdH spot-checks/fan will lock proper settling per investigation Step 3.

Next: Step 2 feasibility (F_L) + Step 3 SdH spot checks at large |n|, D=0.

this device, size Rxx sens off the 8T MR-extrapolated Rxx (~kohm), not the B=0 value

At ~31min/7 rows, sr1 max|V|=109uV > 100uV FS (sens 1e-4): clips at low-n(<~1e12)

Good thing to check first — and it changes the answer. I looked at the QH structure already present in run 5's low-n/high-B corner (the exact region Step 6 targets):

**At n=0.5e12, B=8 T (ν≈2.6): Rxx is stuck at ~4.9–5.5 kΩ with no deep minima**; at n=0.9e12 (ν≈4.2) Rxx min ~2.9 kΩ; at n=1.3e12 (ν≈5.8) ~1.9 kΩ. And R_xy reads a constant ~2.76 kΩ across all three densities (it should scale as h/νe² ≈ 10/6/4 kΩ) — i.e. **the Hall channel is railed** (clipped at the 50 µV FS), and Rxx is partly clipped too. The physics signal that survives the clipping: **Rxx is not dropping toward clean QH minima at ν≈2.6** — the Landau gaps are not well-developed at 8 T / 8 K. That points to modest quantum mobility, the same root cause that gave the high SdH onset.

## Time estimate

| Option | Scope | Time |
|---|---|---|
| **Scout** (recommended first) | n-sweep at fixed B=8 T across n≈0.1–1.5e12, QH-correct sensitivity (sr1/2 ~5e-4, sr3 ~2e-3) — does clean QH form at all? | **~1–1.5 h** (ramp 1→8 T ≈51 min + ~25 min sweep) |
| **Full Step 6** | low-n QH/LL fan (n≈0–1.5e12 × B, Hall, proper sens) for the Streda/zero-mode structure | **~4–5 h** |

So ~1–1.5 h to decide viability; ~5–6.5 h total if you run the full fan after a clean scout.

## Expected conclusion-improvement value

**Moderate, with real risk — and asymmetric.** Honest breakdown:

- **Upside:** Step 6 attacks the exact discriminator (the ABA ML band) through a *different, larger-gap* signature (several-meV LL gaps vs the sub-resolution ~1 T pocket). If clean QH develops, it can be **decisive — especially for ABA**, because `ll_sequence.py` gives a *quantitative, validated* ABA LL/Streda prediction (the non-dispersing N=0 zero-mode doublet + shifted Chern sequence) to match against.
- **Discount 1 — ABC side is qualitative only.** Per the model README, the **quantitative ABC LL model is not built**, so an ABC confirmation (the ν=±6-centred 12-fold zero LL) is a pattern-match, not a fitted overlay → "strong (qualitative)" at best, not decisive.
- **Discount 2 — the data just told us QH is marginal here.** Rxx not reaching minima at ν≈2.6 means the LL gaps aren't cleanly resolved at 8 T/8 K. Step 6 relies on resolving those gaps, so it risks being **limited by the same warm-T/mobility wall** that capped the low-field FS-count. The lowest-ν gap (ν≈2, biggest) is the most likely to survive, so it's not hopeless — but it's not the "free win" the recipe implies for a higher-mobility device.
- **Asymmetry:** much better at *confirming/excluding ABA* than at *positively confirming ABC*.

**My recommendation:** run the **~1–1.5 h scout** first — if Rxx develops clean QH minima and R_xy shows plateaus at the lowest ν, the full Step-6 fan is well worth ~4–5 h and likely decisive (especially if it's ABA). If the scout shows the same smeared, gap-poor QH as run 5's corner, Step 6 won't beat the warm-T wall and the honest move is to **accept the hedged "consistent-with ABC, ABA-not-excluded" call** and flag **lower T (mK rig)** as the real path to a decisive result — that directly resolves the ~1 T ML pocket at low field and would sharpen the QH besides.

# Session notes — QC0426 / vti

Operational log (not a science notebook).

## E1 grant — 2026-06-21
Operator (Zack) granted autonomy: "Ramp down is appropriate. go for autonomy"
once Gate A + Gate B were green and bring-up VERIFY flags addressed. E1 engaged.
First E1 execute = read-only kernel-binding probe (per VERIFY); then magnet
ramp 0.30 T -> 0 T; then Gate C contact liveness -> Step 1 (B=0 gate map / CNP).

## TOOLING — gatemap recipe is toploader-API; no gatemap-vti variant (2026-06-21)
`measurements/gatemap.md` is written in toploader API (`k_tg.volt`, `s.AsyncStation`,
fp temperature). Adapted to VTI for run 0 (Gate C) and the Step-1 map: TG axis =
`dc205_volt` (data col `DC_bias`), set-only param; no TG current monitor so gate
leakage is watched only on `k_bg.curr`/`k_si.curr`; temperature is NOT fp'd
per-point (rig card: LS335 Grafana co-master, per-point poll has killed a run) —
T captured once in `meas_config`. Station built via `async_station(meas_config)`.
A `gatemap-vti` variant capturing these deltas would help.

## PROTOCOL — settling floor vs bring-up dwell (2026-06-21)
Lock-ins read 24 dB/oct, tau=0.3 s (all channels). Rig-card settling floor at
24 dB/oct is k~7-10 tau = 2.1-3 s; the bring-up/Gate C dwell of 4 tau = 1.2 s is
BELOW it, so features can be mildly smeared (small notch at V_bg=0 in run 0).
Reasoning used for Step-1 map: a *constant* fast-axis settling lag shifts the CNP
ridge by the same amount in every row -> biases the intercept (offset) only, NOT
the slope (cap ratio). So the calibration map runs at fast_delay~1.0 s safely for
the ratio; SdH spot-checks/fan will lock proper settling per investigation Step 3.
Did not change filter_slope (operator-owned front-panel setting per rig card).

## FEEDBACK/data — Gate C result (run 0, 2026-06-21)
CNP at TG=0 is V_bg = +0.40 V, peak Rxx ~1.9 kOhm on BOTH sr1(T3-T4) & sr2(B4-B5)
(agree). Geometry-prior cap ratio c_bg/c_tg = t_tg/t_bg = 15.6/12 = 1.30 -> expected
CNP line V_tg ~= -1.30*V_bg + 0.52. Gate leakage at Keithley 1uA-range noise floor
(|I_bg|<=0.24 nA, |I_si|<=0.58 nA), not genuine. Contacts alive.

## Step 1 DONE — (n,D) calibration (run 1, 2026-06-21/22)
B=0 gate map (41x81, 74 min) -> cap ratio c_bg/c_tg = 1.309 (sr1)/1.300 (sr2),
matches geometry prior 1.300 to <1% (happy case, as prior QC0426 campaign noted).
(n=0,D=0) at Vtg=+0.087, Vbg=+0.066. D=0 line reaches >=+/-6e12 cm^-2 in-validators.
Calibration written to device_card.md + ana run-1 block. CNP peak-R grows strongly
with |D| (D-gap, interpretation held). The 24dB/oct fast-axis settling reasoning
held: map vs Gate C slopes agree, offsets differ ~0.27V (settling lag) as predicted.
Next: Step 2 feasibility (F_L) + Step 3 SdH spot checks at large |n|, D=0.

## FEEDBACK/RECIPE FIX — SdH sensitivity vs strong MR (run 2, 2026-06-22)
SC1 (hole, n=-3.5e12, run 2) sr1/sr2 sensitivities (1e-5 = 10uV FS) chosen with
"headroom for MR" CLIPPED above ~4T: Rxx grows ~B^1.8 (49 ohm@0.2T -> 552 ohm@4.4T,
extrap ~1.6 kohm@8T -> 32uV). My MR estimate (~200 ohm@8T) was an order low. The
device has STRONG positive MR at high-|n| metallic. Lesson: for SdH field sweeps on
this device, size Rxx sens off the 8T MR-extrapolated Rxx (~kohm), not the B=0 value
-> use 1e-4 (100uV FS) for sr1/sr2 at n~3.5e12. sdh-spot-check recipe step 3
("full scale ~ I_bias x R_target") should say R_target = the high-B MR value, not B=0.
Also: SdH onset not found below 4.4T (warm electron-T ~8K pushes it high) -> oscillations
live >4T; small 1/B window risks resolution-limited read (investigation anticipates this;
Step 6 Streda fallback). Re-run SC1' rides home 8->1T at sens 1e-4 (no re-traverse).
Also TIMING: uniform-1/B high-B points are EXPENSIVE on the blocking magnet (large dB
per step); SC1 ETA underestimated the high-field tail by ~30min. Price the high-B
traverse explicitly for fans.

## Step 3 HOLE result — resolution-limited (runs 2 clipped + 3 clean, 2026-06-22)
Clean hole-side SdH (run 3, n=-3.5e12, D=0, B 8->1T, sens 1e-4): NO FS count
extractable. Onset high (~3T, warm electron-T ~8K thermally suppresses low-B SdH)
-> short 1/B record -> FFT peak WANDERS across extraction (4/36/19/24T vs cutoff;
10->19T vs bg-degree). Broad ~10-20T blob, no sharp line, ~no power at F_L=36T.
Fork per STYLE rule 14, not a number. Does NOT distinguish ABA vs ABC (both
unresolved). Recorded ana cells 14-17. Electron-side mirror running (run 4). If
both sides limited -> Step-6 high-field Streda/Chern, or resolution-limited
cannot-tell. Step-4 fan NOT yet justified (would inherit the same limitation).
OPERATOR DECISION likely needed on strategic pivot (Step-6 vs report) after run 4.

## Step 3 ELECTRON result — CLEAN, ABC-leaning (run 4, 2026-06-22)
Electron side (n=+3.5e12, D=0, mirror of run 3) is RESOLVABLE: clean periodic SdH,
robust dominant tone ~34T (sr1)/33.5T (sr2), STABLE across cutoff(1.5-4T) & bg-deg(3-7)
[hole wandered 4-36T]. F_L/dom=1.06-1.08 -> tone AT F_L within scale uncertainty =>
single Fermi surface = ABC single-pocket signature (provisional, single density).
Satellites (~6/14/21/30/40/50T) = sidelobe ringing of one tone, not a 2nd pocket.
ABA (f_BL~34T + tiny unresolved f_ML~2T) NOT excluded at this resolution. Recorded
ana cells 18-21. Electron is the clean side.

## Step 4 FAN LAUNCHED — electron D=0 (run 5, 2026-06-22 ~05:00)
landau-fan-vti: n[0.5-3.5]e12 (40 fast) x B[7.95-1.0]T (96 slow, uniform-1/B Nyquist/3
F_L=36T), B descending (rides home from run4 @8T), dwell f2.5/s2, sens 1e-4. ~4.5h.
Per-column SdH FFT -> F(n) vs F_L resolves ABC (single tone tracking F_L) vs ABA
(partition Sigma f = n). The decisive measurement. Checkpoint ~50%.

## FAN clipping at low-n/high-B corner (run 5, ~05:15) — NOT re-running
At ~31min/7 rows, sr1 max|V|=109uV > 100uV FS (sens 1e-4): clips at low-n(<~1e12)
+ high-B(>~6T), i.e. the DEEP-QH corner (n=0.5e12,8T -> nu~2.6, Rxx peak 5528 ohm).
Sized sens off the run-4 spot check (n=3.5e12, Rxx~671 ohm, shallow QH) -> missed the
low-n QH peaks. LESSON: a fan spanning low->high n needs sens for the low-n QH Rxx
(kohm+), not the high-n metallic value; 2e-4 or restrict n>=1e12 would avoid it.
DECISION: continue, NOT re-run. The n>=1.5e12 columns (nu>=8, Rxx<=~1-2kohm) are
CLIP-FREE and carry the decisive F(n)/ABC-vs-ABA read; low-n/high-B is QH (SdH-FFT
invalid there anyway). Analysis: per-column FFT on n>=1.5e12, mask |V|>=99uV points.

## FAN PREVIEW (run 5, 29/96 rows, B>2.6T, df~3.9T) — ABC-consistent (2026-06-22 ~06:20)
Per-column SdH FFT on clean n>=1.5e12: dominant F(n) TRACKS F_L across density,
F_peak/F_L ~ 1.0 +/- 0.1 (1.16 @1.5e12 -> 0.88 @3.5e12, crossing ~1), BOTH channels
(sr1,sr2) agree closely. Sits ON F_L, NOT F_L/2. => single Fermi surface carrying
full Luttinger density => ABC (rhombohedral) leaning/consistent. No partition, no 2nd
branch. Slight ratio slope => small global lever-arm rescale due (pin-the-scale).
PRELIMINARY (partial, coarse df; a small ML partner unresolvable here). Full-res
verdict + Onsager overlay (fs_count_b0) + Luttinger sum at completion (~08:20).
Channels agree => coherent single-domain region (not mosaic).

## CAMPAIGN CALL — fan complete (run 5, 2026-06-22 ~08:30)
Electron-region FS-count: SINGLE Fermi surface tracking F_L across n=1.5-3.5e12,
both channels agree (coherent single domain), Onsager overlay rescale lambda=1.03
(scale prior validated), Luttinger F~=F_L (one 4-fold pocket). => CONSISTENT-WITH
ABC (weak lean). BUT ABA NOT EXCLUDED: model says ABA's ML discriminator pocket is
~0.1-2.2T over this range (fs_count_b0), below this run's resolution (df~1.9T) and in
the MR-background band, and ABA-BL coincides with ABC's tone (~F_L). So the ML partner
is NOT-RESOLVABLE (not searched-and-absent) -> cannot positively distinguish ABA/ABC by
low-field FS-count at this T(~8K electron)/field. Recorded ana cells 22-25 (full output
contract). To FIRM: Step-6 high-field Streda/Chern (dedicated low-n QH run; note ABC LL
model not built -> qualitative ABC side) OR lower T (mK rig) OR n>3.5e12 (extend solver).
Hole side resolution-limited (run3). DELIVERABLE REACHED; Step-6 vs accept = operator call.
Magnet left at 1.0T, device idle, gates on D=0 n-line @ n=0.5e12 (run5 end).

Operational log (not a science notebook).

## E1 grant — 2026-06-21
Operator (Zack) granted autonomy: "Ramp down is appropriate. go for autonomy"
once Gate A + Gate B were green and bring-up VERIFY flags addressed. E1 engaged.
First E1 execute = read-only kernel-binding probe (per VERIFY); then magnet
ramp 0.30 T -> 0 T; then Gate C contact liveness -> Step 1 (B=0 gate map / CNP).

## TOOLING — gatemap recipe is toploader-API; no gatemap-vti variant (2026-06-21)
`measurements/gatemap.md` is written in toploader API (`k_tg.volt`, `s.AsyncStation`,
fp temperature). Adapted to VTI for run 0 (Gate C) and the Step-1 map: TG axis =
`dc205_volt` (data col `DC_bias`), set-only param; no TG current monitor so gate
leakage is watched only on `k_bg.curr`/`k_si.curr`; temperature is NOT fp'd
per-point (rig card: LS335 Grafana co-master, per-point poll has killed a run) —
T captured once in `meas_config`. Station built via `async_station(meas_config)`.
A `gatemap-vti` variant capturing these deltas would help.

## PROTOCOL — settling floor vs bring-up dwell (2026-06-21)
Lock-ins read 24 dB/oct, tau=0.3 s (all channels). Rig-card settling floor at
24 dB/oct is k~7-10 tau = 2.1-3 s; the bring-up/Gate C dwell of 4 tau = 1.2 s is
BELOW it, so features can be mildly smeared (small notch at V_bg=0 in run 0).
Reasoning used for Step-1 map: a *constant* fast-axis settling lag shifts the CNP
ridge by the same amount in every row -> biases the intercept (offset) only, NOT
the slope (cap ratio). So the calibration map runs at fast_delay~1.0 s safely for
the ratio; SdH spot-checks/fan will lock proper settling per investigation Step 3.
Did not change filter_slope (operator-owned front-panel setting per rig card).

## FEEDBACK/data — Gate C result (run 0, 2026-06-21)
CNP at TG=0 is V_bg = +0.40 V, peak Rxx ~1.9 kOhm on BOTH sr1(T3-T4) & sr2(B4-B5)
(agree). Geometry-prior cap ratio c_bg/c_tg = t_tg/t_bg = 15.6/12 = 1.30 -> expected
CNP line V_tg ~= -1.30*V_bg + 0.52. Gate leakage at Keithley 1uA-range noise floor
(|I_bg|<=0.24 nA, |I_si|<=0.58 nA), not genuine. Contacts alive.

## Step 1 DONE — (n,D) calibration (run 1, 2026-06-21/22)
B=0 gate map (41x81, 74 min) -> cap ratio c_bg/c_tg = 1.309 (sr1)/1.300 (sr2),
matches geometry prior 1.300 to <1% (happy case, as prior QC0426 campaign noted).
(n=0,D=0) at Vtg=+0.087, Vbg=+0.066. D=0 line reaches >=+/-6e12 cm^-2 in-validators.
Calibration written to device_card.md + ana run-1 block. CNP peak-R grows strongly
with |D| (D-gap, interpretation held). The 24dB/oct fast-axis settling reasoning
held: map vs Gate C slopes agree, offsets differ ~0.27V (settling lag) as predicted.
Next: Step 2 feasibility (F_L) + Step 3 SdH spot checks at large |n|, D=0.

## FEEDBACK/RECIPE FIX — SdH sensitivity vs strong MR (run 2, 2026-06-22)
SC1 (hole, n=-3.5e12, run 2) sr1/sr2 sensitivities (1e-5 = 10uV FS) chosen with
"headroom for MR" CLIPPED above ~4T: Rxx grows ~B^1.8 (49 ohm@0.2T -> 552 ohm@4.4T,
extrap ~1.6 kohm@8T -> 32uV). My MR estimate (~200 ohm@8T) was an order low. The
device has STRONG positive MR at high-|n| metallic. Lesson: for SdH field sweeps on
this device, size Rxx sens off the 8T MR-extrapolated Rxx (~kohm), not the B=0 value
-> use 1e-4 (100uV FS) for sr1/sr2 at n~3.5e12. sdh-spot-check recipe step 3
("full scale ~ I_bias x R_target") should say R_target = the high-B MR value, not B=0.

live >4T; small 1/B window risks resolution-limited read (investigation anticipates this;
Step 6 Streda fallback). Re-run SC1' rides home 8->1T at sens 1e-4 (no re-traverse).

per step); SC1 ETA underestimated the high-field tail by ~30min. Price the high-B
traverse explicitly for fans.

Clean hole-side SdH (run 3, n=-3.5e12, D=0, B 8->1T, sens 1e-4): NO FS count
extractable. Onset high (~3T, warm electron-T ~8K thermally suppresses low-B SdH)
-> short 1/B record -> FFT peak WANDERS across extraction (4/36/19/24T vs cutoff;
10->19T vs bg-degree). Broad ~10-20T blob, no sharp line, ~no power at F_L=36T.
Fork per STYLE rule 14, not a number. Does NOT distinguish ABA vs ABC (both
unresolved). Recorded ana cells 14-17. Electron-side mirror running (run 4). If
both sides limited -> Step-6 high-field Streda/Chern, or resolution-limited
cannot-tell. Step-4 fan NOT yet justified (would inherit the same limitation).
OPERATOR DECISION likely needed on strategic pivot (Step-6 vs report) after run 4.

## Step 3 ELECTRON result — CLEAN, ABC-leaning (run 4, 2026-06-22)
Electron side (n=+3.5e12, D=0, mirror of run 3) is RESOLVABLE: clean periodic SdH,
robust dominant tone ~34T (sr1)/33.5T (sr2), STABLE across cutoff(1.5-4T) & bg-deg(3-7)
[hole wandered 4-36T]. F_L/dom=1.06-1.08 -> tone AT F_L within scale uncertainty =>
single Fermi surface = ABC single-pocket signature (provisional, single density).
Satellites (~6/14/21/30/40/50T) = sidelobe ringing of one tone, not a 2nd pocket.
ABA (f_BL~34T + tiny unresolved f_ML~2T) NOT excluded at this resolution. Recorded
ana cells 18-21. Electron is the clean side.

F_L=36T), B descending (rides home from run4 @8T), dwell f2.5/s2, sens 1e-4. ~4.5h.
Per-column SdH FFT -> F(n) vs F_L resolves ABC (single tone tracking F_L) vs ABA
(partition Sigma f = n). The decisive measurement. Checkpoint ~50%.

## FAN clipping at low-n/high-B corner (run 5, ~05:15) — NOT re-running
At ~31min/7 rows, sr1 max|V|=109uV > 100uV FS (sens 1e-4): clips at low-n(<~1e12)
+ high-B(>~6T), i.e. the DEEP-QH corner (n=0.5e12,8T -> nu~2.6, Rxx peak 5528 ohm).
Sized sens off the run-4 spot check (n=3.5e12, Rxx~671 ohm, shallow QH) -> missed the
low-n QH peaks. LESSON: a fan spanning low->high n needs sens for the low-n QH Rxx
(kohm+), not the high-n metallic value; 2e-4 or restrict n>=1e12 would avoid it.
DECISION: continue, NOT re-run. The n>=1.5e12 columns (nu>=8, Rxx<=~1-2kohm) are
CLIP-FREE and carry the decisive F(n)/ABC-vs-ABA read; low-n/high-B is QH (SdH-FFT
invalid there anyway). Analysis: per-column FFT on n>=1.5e12, mask |V|>=99uV points.

## FAN PREVIEW (run 5, 29/96 rows, B>2.6T, df~3.9T) — ABC-consistent (2026-06-22 ~06:20)
Per-column SdH FFT on clean n>=1.5e12: dominant F(n) TRACKS F_L across density,
F_peak/F_L ~ 1.0 +/- 0.1 (1.16 @1.5e12 -> 0.88 @3.5e12, crossing ~1), BOTH channels

PRELIMINARY (partial, coarse df; a small ML partner unresolvable here). Full-res

Channels agree => coherent single-domain region (not mosaic).

Electron-region FS-count: SINGLE Fermi surface tracking F_L across n=1.5-3.5e12,

ABC (weak lean). BUT ABA NOT EXCLUDED: model says ABA's ML discriminator pocket is

model not built -> qualitative ABC side) OR lower T (mK rig) OR n>3.5e12 (extend solver).
Hole side resolution-limited (run3). DELIVERABLE REACHED; Step-6 vs accept = operator call.
